extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), their counsel, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, duties, violations, and sanctioning provisions that govern USPTO disciplinary proceedings and enforcement for registered practitioners, including reporting obligations, suspension terms, reinstatement, notice requirements, and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory and regulatory provisions authorize the Office to investigate and impose discipline on registered practitioners; relied upon as the legal basis for the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and applicability of professional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners registered to practice before the Office in patent matters are subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112) and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration status (agent vs. attorney) and registration number are material; practitioners remain bound by these rules while practicing before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report public disciplinary action (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a), a practitioner has a duty to report public discipline imposed by other jurisdictions to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely report public discipline to OED constitutes a violation of the Rules of Professional Conduct (as occurred when Respondent failed to report his 2012 public reproval and 2015 suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report criminal convictions (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(a), practitioners must report criminal convictions to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to report a criminal conviction to OED is a separate reporting obligation and was alleged here for Respondent's 2013 misdemeanor conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: public discipline by state authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may violate the USPTO Rules by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority in a State (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admitted that he 'violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority in the State of California in 2015.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension sanction (one year, deferred start)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for one year, commencing 30 days after the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension includes a 30-day delay before it begins; specific scope covers patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for reinstatement after partial service
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be eligible for reinstatement after serving 30 days of said suspension provided he complies with the terms of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility to seek reinstatement is conditioned on compliance with all terms of the Final Order; actual reinstatement requires an order by the OED Director or USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) and fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: After serving 30 days of suspension, a respondent may file a petition for reinstatement with the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c), accompanied by the fee required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain a statement attesting to compliance with the Final Order, including a sworn declaration that the petitioner has not practiced before the Office during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to jurisdictions (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice, by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the Final Order to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies in which the Respondent is admitted to practice within 30 days of entry of the Final Order, pursuant to § 11.58(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory reporting/notification obligation to other admissions authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to clients with business before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of entry of the Final Order, Respondent shall inform by certified mail, return receipt requested, all of his clients who have immediate or prospective business before the Office of his inability to act on their behalf after the start of his suspension, the need to consult with other counsel, and of any immediate deadlines, pursuant to § 11.58(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: no need to notify a client who, before the start of suspension, has consented to another registered practitioner taking over the representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on practice and communications during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not resume practice before the Office unless and until reinstated; shall not hold himself out as authorized to practice before the Office; shall not advertise availability to perform legal services for anyone with immediate or prospective business before the Office; and shall not render legal advice or services to such persons, unless and until reinstated (pursuant to §§ 11.58(b)(3)–(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions extend to all practice-related representations and advertising concerning business before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limited recognition granted (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is not granted limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly denies any arrangement that would allow limited practice despite suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of compliance steps (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall keep and maintain records of the various steps taken pursuant to the Final Order, pursuant to § 11.58(d), so that in any subsequent proceeding proof of compliance to the Final Order will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintained records are to be sufficient to demonstrate compliance in any future disciplinary or reinstatement proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted non-practitioner activities (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may act as a paralegal or perform other services for another practitioner which are normally performed by laypersons, in conformity with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e) and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits certain limited, non-privileged, layperson-level activities while suspended, so long as they conform to the cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of suspension until formal reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative reinstatement threshold is the OED Director's affirmative grant under the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's reserved rights in reinstatement proceedings (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(e)–(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or the Final Order prevents the OED Director from exercising his rights and obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(e) and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may take actions allowed by the reinstatement provisions, including evidentiary and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (electronic and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; the publication requirement set forth in § 11.60(g) is waived pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.3(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the text of the Official Gazette notice and directs public posting despite the waiver of § 11.60(g).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary investigation, including the Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent; and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor to determine discipline and/or to rebut any statement by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disciplinary record may be used both to aggravate sanctions and to rebut defenses in later matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs in complying with the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No cost-shifting to the other side for compliance-related expenses is ordered.
